claims.text: Thermal oxidation at approximately 600°C promotes formation of a continuous, uniform oxide film on the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Thermally activated oxidation occurs during sliding in the approximately 500–700°C regime.
Microstructural evolution occurs during sliding in the approximately 500–700°C regime.
The oxidation treatment produces a protective, adherent oxide layer.
The treatment may produce grain-boundary enrichment by particular elements.
Grain-boundary elemental enrichment enhances local resistance to wear and deformation.
The induced oxide film acts as a barrier to further oxidation.
The induced oxide film retards dislocation movement during sliding.
Retarding dislocation movement localizes or delays the onset of plastic deformation.
A uniform protective oxide film stabilizes the coating microstructure and inhibits damaging plastic flow.
The thermally oxidized coating will have a lower macroscopic wear rate than the untreated coating during high-temperature sliding.
The thermally oxidized coating will exhibit less microscopic deformation than the untreated coating during high-temperature sliding.
Thermal oxidation will reduce grain-boundary sliding and localized plasticity relative to the untreated coating.
The predicted reductions in wear and deformation are conditional on formation of a uniform and stable oxide film during sliding at 500–700°C.
An excessively thick or non-adherent oxide scale may worsen coating performance.
